title: Nectar's flower, never visited
question: The pale flower at the top of this stem (~22 rows above the soil) never gets a nectar visit across 120,000 frames -- does its height and the water in front of it read as clearly out of an ant's reach, or does it look like it should be gettable?
context_md: B1' (nectar, in two currencies): a flower an animal can afford to feed at now pays out of the plant's own reproductive pocket and stays standing (`plant::nectar_offer`) instead of being bitten off whole. Built and unit-tested -- five green tests exercise every branch directly. But run on the played bed (seed 1, `scenario=played_bed`, 120,000 frames, the colony's own reach 395 of 512 columns), the mechanism never once fires: `flower_visits=0`, `nectar_paid=0` for the whole run. The flower pictured stands behind the pond visible at its base, at the height `Reports/dead-ends.md` line 1636 already recorded as out of an ant's reach (22-40 rows up a stem). `organs_built=87` and `fruit_dropped=14` say the plant side worked normally; nothing ate a flower or a fallen fruit either (`windfall_bitten=0`). This is the same reachability gap the pollinator design (a flitter with a bloom-seeking sense) is being built to close -- not built in this change.
